title: Apple launches official program for leasing Macs as AI price crunch bites — 24- and 36-month leasing options provided by Klarna
summary: Apple launched its Upgrade program in the US, a partnership with Klarna to lease Macs along with iPads, Watches, and iPhones.
body: Following price hikes on the Mac and iPad due to the ongoing memory and storage crisis, Apple has announced a new leasing program, Apple Upgrade. The new offering will be "provided" by Klarna and available in Apple Stores in the U.S., as well as the Apple Store online and the Apple Store app. There will be 24- and 36-month leasing options for the Mac and iPad, while the iPhone and Watch will have 12- and 24-month options. Mac leases will start at $24.99 per month, which includes the MacBook Air , MacBook Pro , iMac, and Mac Studio . Apple's announcement leaves out its cheapest systems, the MacBook Neo and Mac Mini. iPad leases start at $11.99 per month and include the iPad Mini, iPad Air, and iPad Pro, but not the base-level vanilla iPad. body: Physicists at the Universities of Konstanz and Stuttgart have run chaotic-signal forecasting and anomaly detection on 400 microscopic particles orbiting in a drop of liquid, in work published in Communications AI & Computing. The array predicted a chaotic Mackey-Glass series and picked out anomalies that leave a signal's mean, variance, and short-time autocorrelation untouched, scoring an F1 of 0.90 on that harder task. It also came in roughly 10 times less accurate than memristor-based reservoirs , a gap the paper admits candidly. Each oscillator is a silica sphere of 3μm radius, capped on one side with 80nm of carbon and suspended in a water-lutidine mixture held at 28°C. summary: Printed Solid, the Delaware-based filament manufacturer acquired by Czech Prusa Research in 2022, is now known as Prusa USA, Inc.
body: Printed Solid, the Delaware-based filament manufacturer acquired by Czech Prusa Research in 2022, is now known as Prusa USA, Inc. I chatted with Prusa Research team members at Open Sauce, who confirmed the name change was largely window dressing, with nothing changing in the company’s day-to-day operation. Josef Prusa will remain CEO of both companies, with a new Marketing Officer moving up the ranks internally. During the changeover, Printed Solid will be known as “Printed Solid, a Prusa Company”. The website now proudly states that Prusa Research is a “European-American” company with U.S. production capabilities. The company has a duplicate print farm at its 100,000-square-foot Delaware factory for the production of 3D printers and filament. The printers are not yet fully “Made in the USA,” as some parts are still needed from the factory in Prague. This helps overcome supply chain issues for American customers.
